summary: Schmidt–Stix reconstruct hyperbolic curves from relative étale homotopy types over sub-p-adic fields, construct a functorial retraction for smooth geometrically connected varieties over finitely generated extensions of Q that embed into products of hyperbolic curves, prove geometric class preservation in its kernel, and establish anabelian reconstruction for strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods. Absolute and non-geometrically-connected versions use field reconstruction and Kummer theory. The appendix develops coverings, homotopy limits, pointed/unpointed comparisons and pro-classifying spaces. Independent review (2026-09-23) changes this extraction to partial: 93 items, including 19 newly separated dependencies, with remaining atomicity and source-closure gaps. Generic pro-categories are already owned by DiamondsAndVStacks D0; ordinary BG/EG by StableHomotopyKTheory H.1; cohomology by SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2. The pro-model is Isaksen's homotopy-pro-group model, not the strict model. Routes 3, 4, 7 and 8 remain rejected candidates, not accepted ownership allocations. The arithmetic-scheme Chebotarev and general compactification inputs cannot be imported from the originally named layers. Fifteen source-issue records have been independently checked: thirteen confirmed, two rejected; in particular the alleged circular fibre definition was a font-extraction artifact, and the alleged retraction proof gap follows from its established construction. The review does not certify complete prerequisite coverage or formalization.

items.name: Pro-objects and pro-categories
items.statement: For a small filtered category I, an inverse diagram X:I^op → C is a pro-object; equivalently use a covariant functor from a small cofiltered category. Hom_pro-C(X,Y) = lim_j colim_i Hom_C(X_i,Y_j), with composition induced from C. Fix object/index universes before forming pro-C.
items.note: Corrected the filtered/cofiltered variance. D0 already owns pro-categories and must supply their common size-aware carrier. Mathlib's CategoryTheory.Ind at 082e2d3 is a reusable dual construction: do not equate absence of a named Pro declaration with absence of foundational code. Cofinite reindexing is separated below.

items.name: Simplicial sets, pointed objects, simplices, horns, nerves and the abstract model-category carrier
items.statement: SSet is SimplicialObject (Type u); pointed simplicial sets can use Under Δ[0]. The standard cosimplicial simplex, horn subcomplexes, Kan horn-filling predicate, nerve of a small category, and abstract closed-model-category axioms are available. This does not assert a proved Kan–Quillen model-category instance for SSet.
items.note: Read all seven cited declarations at Mathlib 082e2d3. CategoryWithFibrations.lean explicitly marks the full Quillen model structure TODO; an abstract ModelCategory class is not that instance. This bundled library index still needs atomic API decomposition (gap G1).

items.name: Homotopy groups of Kan simplicial sets
items.statement: For a pointed Kan simplicial set (X,x), construct π_n(X,x), with π_0 a pointed set, π_1 a group and π_n abelian for n≥2, functoriality and base-point change; compare with the homotopy groups of its realization.
items.note: Upstream AlgebraicTopology Stage 8(2) explicitly plans the Kan-group construction and topological comparison. Ordinary BG and EG obligations are separated below, not silently inferred from this item.

items.name: Isaksen's homotopy-pro-group model structure, not the strict model structure
items.statement: Use Isaksen (2001), Definition 6.1/Theorem 6.4, on pro-simplicial sets: weak equivalences induce isomorphisms on π_0 and on the homotopy pro-local systems; cofibrations are essentially levelwise cofibrations. Every object is cofibrant. Its pointed version defines Ho(pro-ss_*). This homotopy category is a localization of the strict-model homotopy category, whose weak equivalences are essentially levelwise weak equivalences; the two model structures must not be identified.
items.note: Corrected the extraction's word 'strict'. Read Isaksen Cor. 7.5, Props. 8.2/8.4, Def. 10.1, Prop. 10.6 and Cor. 10.7–10.8, and Prop. 18.4 from https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0106152. Cofibrancy alone does not make every target fibrant.

items.name: Étale topological type and étale homotopy groups
items.statement: For a locally noetherian scheme X, X_et ∈ pro-ss is obtained by applying the connected-component functor to the cofiltered system of rigid étale hypercovers (Friedlander). A geometric point x̄ gives a point x̄_et, and π_n^et(X, x̄) := π_n(X_et, x̄_et). For X locally noetherian, π_1^et is the SGA 3 X §6 étale fundamental group, whose profinite completion is the SGA 1 group; if X is noetherian and geometrically unibranch these pro-groups are profinite (Artin–Mazur 11.1). For a field k, G_k = π_1(k_et, K_et).
items.note: Use rigid hypercovers, not arbitrary choices of ordinary hypercovers without a cofinality comparison. Mathlib's scheme étale site and generic sheaf cohomology are partial inputs already recorded in AUDIT-01 SF.2; EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2 owns generic hypercovers/descent, not this rigid topological-type comparison.

items.name: Étale homotopy exact sequence for a geometric fibration (Friedlander, Thm. 11.5)
items.statement: Let f:X→Y be an elementary fibration of smooth connected varieties over a characteristic-zero field, with geometric points x̄↦ȳ. Let 𝒴 be the inverse system of pointed finite étale Galois covers of Y and 𝒳 its pullback to X. Friedlander 11.5, with all primes, supplies the fibre homotopy exact sequence for X_ȳ,𝒳,𝒴; finite-cover invariance of π_n for n≥2 identifies it with ⋯→π_n^et(X_ȳ)→π_n^et(X)→π_n^et(Y)→π_(n−1)^et(X_ȳ)→⋯. In particular, if Y is K(π,1), 1→π_1^et(X_ȳ)→π_1^et(X)→π_1^et(Y)→1 is exact.
items.note: Restricted to the application actually used in Proposition 2.8. Do not export an all-characteristic elementary-fibration theorem or the unspecified phrase 'satisfies Friedlander's hypotheses'. Primary Friedlander proof closure remains G3.

items.name: Remark 1.4(2): étale realization factors through A¹-homotopy theory
items.statement: In the characteristic-zero setting of the introduction, étale realization on smooth k-schemes factors through the Morel–Voevodsky A¹-homotopy category as in Remark 1.4(ii); hence it is not faithful on all smooth schemes. A positive-characteristic extension requires the prime-to-characteristic/completed target specified by Isaksen, not unchanged full étale homotopy.
items.note: Corrected page and characteristic scope. Isaksen's cited Theorem 2.6/Cor. 2.7 explicitly use a Z/p-cohomological target for p invertible on the base. The comparison giving the paper's uncompleted characteristic-zero formulation is a separate proof obligation, not discharged by that citation alone (G3). This remark is not used in §§2–7.

items.name: Lemma 2.1: finite étale morphisms give finite coverings of étale types
items.statement: If p: W′ → W is finite étale, then p_et: W′_et → W_et is a finite covering in pro-ss, and for any X → W the natural map (X ×_W W′)_et → X_et ×_{W_et} W′_et is an isomorphism in pro-ss.

items.name: Lemma 2.2: base change of homotopy equivalences along finite étale maps
items.statement: Let f: X → W, g: Y → W and γ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(X_et, Y_et) with g_et γ = f_et. For W′ → W finite étale there is γ′ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)((X ×_W W′)_et, (Y ×_W W′)_et) compatible with γ and with the projections to W′_et (γ′ is not asserted to be unique).
items.note: From Lemma 2.1 and Proposition A.6.

items.name: Proposition 2.3: Galois-equivariant comparison of geometric cohomology
items.statement: Let X, Y be varieties over k with X_et ≅ Y_et in Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et. Then there are G_k-isomorphisms H^i_et(X_k̄, A) ≅ H^i_et(Y_k̄, A), functorial in the abelian group A, for all i ≥ 0.
items.note: The proof identifies (X ×_k k̄)_et with X_et ×_{k_et} (k′_et)_{k′⊂k̄} via limits of étale cohomology and the cohomological criterion, then applies Proposition A.6.

items.name: Strongly center-free profinite groups; sub-p-adic fields (Mochizuki, Lemma 15.8)
items.statement: A profinite group is strongly center-free if every open subgroup has trivial center. A sub-p-adic field is a subfield of a finitely generated extension of Q_p. Absolute Galois groups of sub-p-adic fields (in particular of finitely generated extensions of Q) are strongly center-free (Mochizuki, Invent. Math. 138 (1999), Lemma 15.8).
items.note: Proved in Mochizuki's local pro-p anabelian paper; it belongs with the Mochizuki reconstruction theorem.

items.name: Proposition 2.4(a): lifting maps and isomorphisms over k_et
items.statement: Let X,Y be connected varieties over k, with Y geometrically connected and geometrically unibranch. Choose geometric points over a common separably closed K/k, with k̄ the separable closure of k in K. Forgetting points gives a surjection Hom_Ho(pro-ss_*)↓(k_et,k̄_et)((X_et,x̄_et),(Y_et,ȳ_et)) → Hom_Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et(X_et,Y_et); isomorphisms lift to isomorphisms.
items.note: From Theorems A.8, A.13 and Lemma A.12.

items.name: Corollaries 2.5–2.6: induced outer homomorphisms and π₁-open maps
items.statement: For X, Y as in Proposition 2.4, OutHom_{G_k}(π_1^et(X), π_1^et(Y)) := Hom_{G_k}(π_1^et(X, x̄), π_1^et(Y, ȳ))_{π_1^et(Y_k̄, ȳ)} is independent of base points, and Mor_k(X, Y) → OutHom_{G_k} factors through Mor_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) when G_k is strongly center-free (Corollary 2.5). With Mor^{π_1-open} the maps whose π_1 has open image, the pointed π_1-open maps modulo π_1^et(Y_k̄, ȳ) biject with the unpointed π_1-open maps (Corollary 2.6).

items.name: Varieties of type K(π,1) and Lemma 2.7
items.statement: A geometrically pointed connected locally noetherian scheme (X, x̄) is of type K(π,1) if π_n^et(X, x̄) = 0 for all n ≥ 2, equivalently the classifying morphism (X_et, x̄_et) → Bπ_1(X_et, x̄_et) is an isomorphism in Ho(pro-ss_*); for geometrically unibranch X this is independent of the base point. Lemma 2.7: (1) a connected smooth curve over a field that is affine or of genus > 0 is of type K(π,1) (Schmidt, Compositio 1996, Prop. 15); (2) over a characteristic-zero field a product of geometrically connected, geometrically unibranch varieties of type K(π,1) is of type K(π,1).
items.note: Part (2) uses the Künneth formulas for π_1 (SGA 1 XIII 4.6) and étale cohomology, and the cohomological criterion (Artin–Mazur 4.3).

items.name: Proposition 2.8: elementary fibrations preserve K(π,1)
items.statement: An elementary fibration X → Y is the complement, in a smooth proper curve X̄ → Y with geometrically connected fibres, of a divisor D finite étale over Y with affine fibres X → Y. Over a field of characteristic zero, if f: X → Y is an elementary fibration of smooth varieties and Y is of type K(π,1), then X is of type K(π,1), and 1 → π_1^et(X_ȳ) → π_1^et(X) → π_1^et(Y) → 1 is exact.

items.name: Existence of Artin's good neighbourhoods (SGA 4 XI 3.3)
items.statement: For a smooth variety X of dimension d with a projective compactification X ⊆ X̄ ⊆ P(V) (X̄ normal, O(1)|_X̄ an r-th multiple, r ≥ 2), the linear projections from general Δ_W, W ∈ Grass_d(V), restricted over a non-empty open S_W ⊆ P(W), are elementary fibrations U_W → S_W; over an algebraically closed field every point lies in some U_W.
items.note: The paper applies SGA 4 XI 3.3 over an infinite perfect field at a rational point, then descends from k̄ to k.

items.name: Lemma 2.9: maps into products of K(π,1) varieties are componentwise
items.statement: Let k have characteristic zero with G_k strongly center-free, X a k-variety and Y_1, Y_2 geometrically connected, geometrically unibranch k-varieties of type K(π,1). Then Hom_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, (Y_1 ×_k Y_2)_et) → Hom(X_et, Y_{1,et}) × Hom(X_et, Y_{2,et}) is bijective.

items.name: Künneth formula for étale fundamental groups in characteristic zero (SGA 1 XIII 4.6)
items.statement: For geometrically connected varieties Y_1, Y_2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, π_1^et(Y_1 × Y_2) ≅ π_1^et(Y_1) × π_1^et(Y_2); hence over any characteristic-zero k, π_1^et(Y_1 ×_k Y_2) ≅ π_1^et(Y_1) ×_{G_k} π_1^et(Y_2).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 2.7(2) and Lemma 2.9, pp. 827–828
items.note: IG.1 keeps the geometric/arithmetic fundamental-group sequence in the selected SGA range.

items.name: Künneth formula for étale cohomology (SGA 4½, Th. finitude, Cor. 1.11)
items.statement: For smooth separated finite-type varieties X,Y over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k and a prime ℓ, the external product gives H^m_et(X×_kY,F_ℓ) ≅ ⊕_(a+b=m) H^a_et(X,F_ℓ)⊗_(F_ℓ)H^b_et(Y,F_ℓ). General finite coefficients require the derived/Tor form or reduction arguments, not the displayed field-coefficient tensor formula.
items.note: The coefficient-field specialization used in the K(π,1) argument is written explicitly. Do not silently replace arbitrary finite abelian coefficients by a Tor-free tensor product.

items.name: Definition A.1: coverings and Galois coverings of pro-spaces
items.statement: A map of simplicial sets p: Y → X is a covering if every Δ[0] → Y over Δ[n] → X lifts uniquely (Gabriel–Zisman); coverings lift uniquely against horns and are fibrations; a connected covering is Galois with group Aut_X(Y) if Y/Aut_X(Y) ≅ X. A morphism of pro-spaces is a covering (resp. Galois covering) if it is isomorphic to a level-wise one. A pointed connected pro-space has a pointed universal covering (the system of level-wise universal coverings), which is Galois with group π_1(X, x).

items.name: Proposition A.2: the covering associated with a sub-pro-group
items.statement: For (X, x) connected in Ho(pro-ss_*) and a monomorphism of pro-groups U ↪ π_1(X, x), there is (X, x)_U → (X, x) in Ho(pro-ss_*)_c such that for every connected (W, w), [(W, w), (X, x)_U] ≅ {f ∈ [(W, w), (X, x)] : π_1(f) factors through U}.
items.note: The ambient category in Proposition A.2 is pointed, with connected objects: correct the omitted star in the preceding definition (E12).

items.name: Lemmas A.3–A.5: coverings, fibrations and properness
items.statement: Lemma A.3: pull-back along a weak equivalence of connected pro-spaces is an equivalence of categories of connected coverings. Lemma A.4: coverings are fibrations in pro-ss. Lemma A.5: for a fibration W′ → W and a weak equivalence h: Y → X over W, h × id: Y ×_W W′ → X ×_W W′ is a weak equivalence (properness; Hirschhorn 13.3.2).

items.name: Proposition A.6: base change of homotopy equivalences along coverings
items.statement: Let f: X → W, g: Y → W be maps of pro-spaces and γ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(X, Y) with gγ = f. For a covering W′ → W there is γ′ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(X ×_W W′, Y ×_W W′) compatible with γ and the projections to W′, functorial in W′; for a Galois covering of connected pro-spaces the induced isomorphisms H^i(Y ×_W W′, A) → H^i(X ×_W W′, A) are G(W′/W)-equivariant.

items.name: Lemma A.7: derived limits of profinite pro-groups vanish
items.statement: For a pro-finite group G = (G_i), lim¹ G = * (Bousfield–Kan's non-abelian lim¹); for a pro-finite abelian group, lim^s G = 0 for all s ≥ 1.
items.note: Via the strongly Mittag-Leffler pro-group G*_i = ∏_{j≤i} G_j and compactness.

items.name: Theorem A.8: topological homotopy groups of profinite pro-spaces
items.statement: Define π_n^top(X, x) := π_n(holim X) = Mor_{Ho(pro-ss_*)}((S^n, s_n), (X, x)) and call (X, x) path-connected if π_0^top = *. If π_0(X, x) = * and all π_n(X, x) are pro-finite, then π_n^top(X, x) → lim π_n(X, x) is an isomorphism for all n ≥ 0.
items.note: Theorem A.8 is an isomorphism of underlying groups (pointed sets in degree 0), not a newly declared topology. The Bousfield–Kan proof must correct the cosimplicial-degree/partial-totalization confusion in E9.

items.name: Lemma A.9, Theorem A.10 and Corollary A.11: pointed versus unpointed classes
items.statement: Paths in a fibrant approximation give a well-defined associative action π_1^top(Y, y_0, y_1) × [(X, x), (Y, y_0)]_* → [(X, x), (Y, y_1)]_* (Lemma A.9). If Y is path-connected, forgetting base points induces a bijection ([(X, x), (Y, y)]_*)_{π_1^top(Y, y)} ≅ [X, Y] (Theorem A.10). If X ≅ Y in Ho(pro-ss) and all π_i(Y, y) are pro-finite, then (X, x) ≅ (Y, y) in Ho(pro-ss_*) (Corollary A.11).
items.locator: Lemma A.9, Theorem A.10 and Corollary A.11, p. 859
items.note: A.9/A.10 require the actual monodromy action and orbit argument, not an assertion of injectivity before quotienting. Use the weak-equivalence cylinder, correcting E10–E11; its projection need not be a fibration.

items.name: Lemma A.12: the monodromy action is conjugation on π₁
items.statement: For pointed connected pro-spaces, the π_1^top(Y, y)-action on Hom(π_1^top(X, x), π_1^top(Y, y)) induced by α ↦ α(id_Y) is φ ↦ α φ(−) α^{−1}; the orbits are the outer homomorphisms.

items.name: Theorem A.13: pointed versus unpointed over a base
items.statement: Let (X, x), (Y, y) be pointed pro-spaces over (B, b) with Y, B path-connected and π_1^top(Y, y) → π_1^top(B, b) surjective. (a) Forgetting base points gives a surjection Mor_{Ho(pro-ss_*)↓(B,b)}((X, x), (Y, y)) ↠ Mor_{Ho(pro-ss)↓B}(X, Y), and isomorphisms lift to isomorphisms. (b) With S_X ⊆ π_1^top(B, b) the stabilizer of the structure map of (X, x) and Δ_{X,Y} its preimage in π_1^top(Y, y), the map on Δ_{X,Y}-orbits is a bijection.
items.locator: Theorem A.13, p. 860; proof as corrected by E5
items.note: Use the relative Hom sets in equations (9)–(10), correcting E13, and the target base point y (E5).

items.name: Pro-classifying spaces: BG, EG and the fibrant model B*G (Lemma A.14)
items.statement: For a pro-group G, BG and EG are defined level-wise; EG is contractible and EG_i → BG_i is a G_i-covering, but BG need not be fibrant. With G* = (∏_{j≤i} G_j)_i and B*G := EG*/G, B*G is fibrant in pro-ss_* and BG → B*G is a weak equivalence (Lemma A.14).

items.name: Lemma A.15 and Proposition A.16: BG represents Hom(π₁(−), G)
items.statement: For pro-groups G, G′, the maps Hom(G′, G) → Hom_{pro-ss_*}(BG′, BG) → Hom_{Ho(pro-ss_*)}(BG′, BG) → Hom(G′, G) are all bijections (Lemma A.15). For a connected pointed pro-space (X, x) and a pro-group G, π_1(−): Mor_{Ho(pro-ss_*)}((X, x), BG) → Mor_{pro-groups}(π_1(X, x), G) is a functorial bijection (Proposition A.16).
items.locator: Lemma A.15 and Proposition A.16, pp. 863–864
items.note: Uses the fundamental groupoid nerve BΠX and the level-wise covering B*G → BG*.

items.name: Definition A.17 and Corollary A.18: classifying morphism and K(π,1) pro-spaces
items.statement: The classifying morphism of a pointed connected pro-space is the map (X, x) → Bπ_1(X, x) in Ho(pro-ss_*) corresponding to the identity of π_1 under Proposition A.16; (X, x) is of type K(π,1) if π_i(X, x) = 0 for i ≥ 2, which holds iff the classifying morphism is an isomorphism (Corollary A.18, via Isaksen Cor. 7.5).
items.locator: Definition A.17 and Corollary A.18, p. 866

items.name: Hyperbolic curves and the conventions of the paper
items.statement: All schemes are separated and locally noetherian; an immersion is an open followed by a closed immersion; an étale covering is a finite étale morphism; a variety is a scheme of finite type over a field. A hyperbolic curve over k is a geometrically connected (smooth) curve C with χ(C_k̄, Q_ℓ) < 0, i.e. 2g − 2 + n > 0 for genus g and n geometric boundary points.
items.note: NC.1 plans only smooth proper hyperbolic curves over number fields; the affine hyperbolic curves over general fields used throughout are part of the new Part II's carrier.

items.name: Theorem 3.1: Mochizuki's Hom theorem for sub-p-adic fields (Theorem A)
items.statement: Let k be sub-p-adic, X a smooth connected k-variety and Y a smooth hyperbolic curve over k. For any geometric base points, Mor_k^dom(X, Y) → Mor^open_{G_k}(π_1^et(X, x̄), π_1^et(Y, ȳ))_{π_1^et(Y_k̄, ȳ)} is bijective, where Mor^dom are dominant k-morphisms and Mor^open_{G_k} are continuous G_k-homomorphisms with open image.
items.locator: Theorem 3.1, p. 829 (Mochizuki, Invent. Math. 138 (1999), Thm. A)
items.note: NC.1 plans a Mochizuki reconstruction theorem for smooth proper hyperbolic curves over number fields and states that the Hom version and the affine variants need their own sources; this is that source. Also used over the function field of Y in Theorem 6.2.

items.name: Tamagawa: distinct rational points have non-conjugate decomposition groups (Cor. 2.10)
items.statement: Let C be a smooth proper curve of genus ≥ 1 over a finite field F. The decomposition subgroups in π_1^et(C) of distinct F-rational points are not conjugate; consequently for each w ∈ C(F) there is a connected étale covering C′ → C, geometrically connected, with an F-point over w and none over any other F-point of C.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.6, pp. 834–835 (Tamagawa, Compositio 109 (1997), Cor. 2.10)
items.note: Non-conjugacy and separation of a rational point by a finite étale cover are distinct obligations. The paper's actual statement is h(C′(F))={w}, not that C′(F) consists of exactly one point. Retain compactness/open-subgroup separation.

items.name: Pop's birational anabelian theorem for finitely generated fields over Q
items.statement: For finitely generated extension fields k, ℓ of Q, Isom(Spec k, Spec ℓ) → OutIsom(G_k, G_ℓ) ≅ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(k_et, ℓ_et) is a bijection (Pop, Ann. of Math. 139 (1994); Pop, Progr. Math. 181 (2000)).
items.note: The field-reconstruction case of source-qualified anabelian reconstruction; nothing in the atlas plans it.

items.name: Galois groups of Hilbertian fields have no nontrivial finitely generated closed normal subgroups
items.statement: Finitely generated extensions of Q are Hilbertian, and the absolute Galois group of a Hilbertian field has no nontrivial finitely generated closed normal subgroup (Fried–Jarden, Field Arithmetic, 3rd ed., Prop. 16.11.6).
items.note: The paper cites FJ08 16.11.6 for this consequence; independent review has not read the cited book proposition and does not certify its full Hilbertian-field formulation. The checked Mochizuki 2006 Theorem 2.4 passage proves the number-field case with further ingredients. Route 3 is rejected until the exact source range and ownership beyond IG.2's ordinary HIT are resolved (G2).

items.name: Finite generation of geometric fundamental groups in characteristic zero
items.statement: For a smooth geometrically connected variety X over a characteristic-zero field k, its geometric étale fundamental group π_1^et(X_k̄,x̄) is topologically finitely generated. It is the kernel of π_1^et(X,x̄)→G_k.
items.note: Use only the smooth application in Theorem 7.1. Correct the bibliography: [Gro72] is SGA 7 I, Exposé II, Thm. 2.3.1, not SGA 7 II. An arbitrary nonsmooth variant needs its own source hypotheses.

items.name: Chebotarev detection on regular arithmetic models
items.statement: For a connected finite étale Galois cover 𝒴→𝒳 with group G, where 𝒳 is nonempty regular connected, finite type and flat over Z as in the models of §§5.1–5.2, each conjugacy class in G occurs as a closed-point Frobenius class. Equivalently, after choosing a point above the closed point one can realize any prescribed element of G as its Frobenius.
items.note: Restricted to the paper's arithmetic-model application. The original assertion for an arbitrary finite-type Z-scheme is false: Spec F_p with connected constant cover of degree >1 has only one closed point. A general density-zero statement requires a specified density and further source hypotheses; removed. Primary Serre theorem/ownership closure is gap G4.

items.name: Closed points of schemes of finite type over Z: Jacobson property and finite residue fields
items.statement: A scheme of finite type over Z is Jacobson: every closed subset is the closure of its closed points. Thus a locally closed subset containing every closed point is the whole space. This does not mean that the union of singleton closures of closed points contains generic points.
items.note: Corrected the false union-of-closures claim. Read Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace and MvPolynomial.comp_C_integral_of_surjective_of_isJacobsonRing at the pin; both require a Jacobson base. No ℤ-specific IsJacobsonRing instance was located by declaration/text searches.

items.name: Spreading out over a regular base of finite type over Z
items.statement: Given finitely many varieties, morphisms, immersions, smooth compactifications with strict normal crossing boundary and finite étale coverings over a finitely generated field k/Q, there is a regular connected scheme S of finite type over Z with function field k over which all of them extend with the same properties.
items.locator: Proofs of Propositions 4.4, 5.1 and Lemma 5.2, pp. 833, 839–840
items.note: The standard EGA IV §8 limit arguments, used without statement in the paper.

items.name: Resolution of singularities and normal-crossings compactification in characteristic zero
items.statement: Over a field of characteristic zero, smooth varieties X, Y with morphisms to a proper W have smooth compactifications X̄, Ȳ with simple normal crossing boundary to which the morphisms extend.
items.note: The cited R09.7/R09.7d plans smooth quasi-projective compactification, not the unrestricted smooth X of Proposition 4.4. Its library audit does not close general compactification plus extension of maps to proper W. Keep this wider dependency unresolved and do not advertise it as supplied; see G5.

items.name: Relative purity for a strict normal crossing divisor
items.statement: For j: X ↪ X̄ the complement of a relative strict normal crossing divisor D = ∪ D_α over S and ℓ invertible on S, R^b j_* Q_ℓ = Λ^b R^1 j_* Q_ℓ ≅ ⊕_{|J|=b} i_{J,*} Q_ℓ(−b) (Gabber's work, Exp. XVI Cor. 3.1.3).
items.note: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.2 plans the smooth trace and relative purity.

items.name: Smooth and proper base change, and local constancy of higher direct images
items.statement: For proper smooth morphisms the sheaves R^a f_* Q_ℓ are smooth (SGA 4½ Arcata V 3.1); smooth sheaves on a normal connected S give π_1^et(S)-representations with cospecialisation isomorphisms, and compactly supported cohomology commutes with base change.
items.note: SF.2 plans proper/smooth base change and compact support.

items.name: Poincaré duality for smooth varieties
items.statement: For a smooth separated finite-type variety X of pure dimension d over a separably closed field of characteristic different from ℓ, the pairing H^i_et(X,Q_ℓ) × H_c^(2d−i)(X,Q_ℓ) → Q_ℓ(−d) is perfect. If X and its structures descend to a field, this pairing is equivariant for its Galois action.
items.note: EDC.2:pairings explicitly supplies the compact-support, twist and equivariance forms. Added ℓ invertible and descent qualification.

items.name: Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula
items.statement: For X separated of finite type over F_q and ℓ≠char F_q, |X(F_q)| = Σ_i (−1)^i tr(Frob_q | H_c^i(X_Fqbar,Q_ℓ)), where Frob_q is geometric Frobenius.
items.note: SF.2 imports the point-counting supplier rather than recreating six operations. Geometric versus arithmetic Frobenius is fixed explicitly; /54 uses arithmetic Frobenius and the factor q^d.

items.name: Lifting étale coverings from a closed fibre to a Nisnevich neighbourhood
items.statement: Let S be locally noetherian, W→S proper, and s a closed point of S. A finite étale cover of W_s extends to a finite étale cover of W_T after a Nisnevich neighborhood (T,t)→(S,s), with κ(t)=κ(s).
items.note: Retain the noetherian/finite-presentation setting needed by proper henselian lifting and descent. The concrete use has S regular finite type over Z. IG.1 owns the cover-specialization comparison; not a statement for an arbitrary improper family.

items.name: Riemann–Hurwitz for tame coverings of curves
items.statement: Let C′→C be a finite étale map of degree d between smooth geometrically connected curves over an algebraically closed field, extending to a finite map of their smooth proper compactifications, tamely ramified at the boundary. If g,g′ are compactification genera and n,n′ the numbers of boundary points, then 2g′−2+n′ = d(2g−2+n).
items.note: Added finite étale over the open curve: tameness at infinity alone does not exclude interior ramification. Import the different/Hurwitz theorem from AlgebraicCurves Layer 7; the punctured-curve formula is its explicitly stated corollary.

items.name: Elementary abelian ℓ-coverings of the projective line minus n points
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k, let ℓ be prime with ℓ≠char k, and let C=P¹_k minus n distinct points, with n≥3. The maximal elementary abelian ℓ-quotient of π_1^et(C) is F_ℓ^(n−1), and the boundary inertia images are nonzero pairwise distinct lines, with the single sum relation.
items.note: Corrected n≥1 to n≥3. For n=1 the group is zero; for n=2 both inertia lines coincide. IG.3's characteristic-zero Riemann-existence construction alone does not supply the positive-characteristic prime-to-ℓ assertion; route this as a tame fundamental-group source in IG.1.

items.name: Isom schemes of elementary fibrations in hyperbolic curves are finite unramified
items.statement: For an elementary fibration of smooth connected characteristic-zero varieties X→Y whose fibres are hyperbolic curves, the relative scheme Isom_Y(X,X) is finite and unramified over Y. As Y is normal integral, each section over its function field K extends uniquely to a section over Y.
items.note: Normality of the base is essential to the generic-section extension, not a consequence of 'finite unramified' alone. Deligne–Mumford 1.11 on p. 84 is stated for proper stable curves; the affine family needs the finite-étale boundary/marked-curve adapter. R09.2 owns this adapter, not an unqualified citation to unmarked stable curves (G6).

items.name: Kummer theory for Galois cohomology
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero field k and an integer n≥1, continuous Galois cohomology with the natural cyclotomic action on μ_n satisfies H¹(k,μ_n) ≅ k×/(k×)^n. Naturality uses a field homomorphism together with a compatible embedding of separable closures.
items.note: Tau Ceti's FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Kummer.lean already constructs the Kummer map, its root-cocycle formula and an injection of power classes. Its docstring explicitly leaves Hilbert-90 surjectivity open. Import those results and build only the remaining isomorphism/naturality under ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9.

items.name: Profinite groups, absolute Galois groups and compactness arguments
items.statement: Absolute Galois groups with the Krull topology and the category of profinite groups with continuous homomorphisms are available. A nonempty downward-directed family of nonempty closed subsets of a compact space, with a compact member, has nonempty intersection. These are carrier/compactness inputs, not every open/closed-subgroup lemma subsequently used.
items.locator: §1, p. 821; proofs of Lemma 5.2, Proposition 5.3, Lemma 5.6, pp. 840–844
items.note: Mathlib: Field.absoluteGaloisGroup, krullTopology, ProfiniteGrp, IsCompact.nonempty_iInter_of_directed_nonempty_isCompact_isClosed.

items.name: Theorem 3.2: dominant Hom reconstruction in homotopy form
items.statement: For a prime p, a sub-p-adic field k, a smooth connected k-variety X and a smooth hyperbolic k-curve Y, Hom_k^dom(X,Y) → Hom_Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et^(π_1-open)(X_et,Y_et) is bijective.
items.note: From Theorem 3.1, Proposition 2.4 and Proposition A.16 (hyperbolic curves are K(π,1) by Lemma 2.7).

items.name: Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 1.3: the retraction
items.statement: Let k be finitely generated over Q and X, Y smooth geometrically connected k-varieties that embed as locally closed subschemes in products of hyperbolic curves. Then Isom_k(X, Y) → Isom_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) is a split injection with a functorial retraction r (Theorem 1.2). In particular X_et ≅ Y_et in Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et implies X ≅ Y (Corollary 1.3).
items.note: Proved as Theorem 4.7.

items.name: Proposition 4.1: point counts in closed fibres from generic-fibre cohomology
items.statement: Let S be normal integral noetherian, s ∈ S closed with finite residue field F_s of size N(s), ℓ invertible on S, X̄ → S proper smooth of relative dimension d and X ⊆ X̄ the complement of a relative strict normal crossing divisor with smooth components. Then the G_{κ(η)}-action on H^i(X_η̄, Q_ℓ) factors through π_1^et(S, η̄), and |X_s(F_s)| = N(s)^d Σ_{i=0}^{2d} (−1)^i tr(φ_s | H^i_et(X_η̄, Q_ℓ)), with φ_s the arithmetic Frobenius.
items.note: The argument is componentwise if S is not connected; an integral S provides the generic point η used in the statement. Arithmetic Frobenius acts on H¹(G_m,Q_ℓ)=Q_ℓ(−1) by q^−1, so q(1−q^−1)=q−1.

items.name: Definition 4.2: factor-dominant immersions
items.statement: An immersion ι: Y ↪ W = C_1 × ⋯ × C_n into a product of smooth geometrically connected curves is factor-dominant if every p_i ι is dominant. For Y geometrically connected and geometrically reduced each p_i ι is dominant or constant with k-rational image, so constant factors can be removed.

items.name: Proposition 4.3: morphisms to the ambient product from étale types
items.statement: Let k be sub-p-adic, ι: Y ↪ W = C_1 × ⋯ × C_n a factor-dominant immersion of a geometrically connected, geometrically unibranch k-variety into a product of hyperbolic curves, and X smooth connected. For every π_1-open γ: X_et → Y_et in Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et there is a unique k-morphism f: X → W with f_et = ι_et γ.
items.note: From Theorem 3.2 and Lemma 2.9.

items.name: Proposition 4.4 and Remark 4.5: the morphism factors through Y
items.statement: Let k be finitely generated over Q, ι: Y ↪ W a smooth locally closed subscheme of a product of hyperbolic curves, X smooth and f: X → W with f_et = ι_et γ for some γ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(X_et, Y_et). Then f = ι g for a unique g: X → Y. (Remark 4.5: g_et also satisfies the diagram, but γ = g_et is not claimed.)
items.note: Reduces to Proposition 4.6 after passing to covers with genus ≥ 2 compactifications, compactifying and spreading out.

items.name: Proposition 4.6: Tamagawa's point-count argument
items.statement: Let S be regular connected of finite type over Z, C_i → S proper smooth curves with geometrically connected fibres of genus ≥ 1, ι: Y ↪ W = ∏_S C_i a locally closed subscheme smooth over S, and f: X → W an S-morphism with X/S smooth, where X and Y have nice relative compactifications mapping to W. If (f_η)_et = (ι_η)_et γ for some γ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)((X_η)_et, (Y_η)_et), then f factors through Y.
items.note: The cover has image h(W′_s(F))={f(x)}, not necessarily W′_s(F) a singleton. The equality |Y′_s(F)|=q^(d_Y−d_X)|X′_s(F)| implies nonemptiness; no equality of dimensions is assumed.

items.name: Theorem 4.7: the unique functorial retraction
items.statement: For k finitely generated over Q and X, Y smooth geometrically connected varieties embeddable in products of hyperbolic curves, (−)_et: Isom_k(X, Y) → Isom_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) admits a unique functorial retraction r such that (a) r(g_et) = g for every k-isomorphism g; (b) r(γ_2 γ_1) = r(γ_2) r(γ_1) for a further smooth geometrically connected such Z; and (c) h_et r(γ)_et = h_et γ for every dominant h: Y → C to a hyperbolic curve. r(γ) is independent of the chosen immersion.
items.locator: Theorem 4.7, pp. 835–837; statement and proof as corrected by E1–E2
items.note: r(γ) is built from Propositions 4.3–4.4; it is an isomorphism formally from (a) and (b).

items.name: Proposition 4.8: compatibility of r with dominant maps
items.statement: For k finitely generated over Q and X, X′, Y, Y′ smooth geometrically connected k-varieties embeddable in products of hyperbolic curves, dominant k-morphisms f: X′ → X, g: Y′ → Y and isomorphisms γ′, γ with γ f_et = g_et γ′, one has g r(γ′) = r(γ) f.

items.name: Theorem 1.9 and class-preserving automorphisms
items.statement: For 1 → H → G → Γ → 1, φ ∈ Aut_Γ(G) is class-preserving by elements of H if φ(g) ∈ {hgh^{−1} : h ∈ H} for every g. Theorem 1.9: for k finitely generated over Q, X smooth geometrically connected and embeddable in a product of hyperbolic curves, and γ in the kernel of r: Aut_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et) → Aut_k(X), the outer automorphism π_1(γ) ∈ OutAut_{G_k}(π_1^et(X)) is class-preserving by elements of π_1^et(X_k̄).
items.note: Assembled from Propositions 5.1, 5.3, 5.5 and Lemma 5.6.

items.name: Proposition 5.1: normality under hypothesis (NR)
items.statement: Let X be as in Theorem 1.9 with a factor-dominant immersion ι: X ↪ ∏ C_i such that (NR) no C_i is rational. For γ ∈ Aut_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et) with r(γ) = id_X, φ = π_1(γ) maps every open normal subgroup N of π_1^et(X) to itself.
items.note: Via ι_et γ = ι_et, Proposition A.2, Čebotarev for schemes and the argument of Proposition 4.6 applied to X_N and X_φ(N).

items.name: Lemma 5.2: automorphisms send elements to conjugates of powers
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 5.1, a pointed lift φ ∈ Aut_{G_k}(π_1^et(X, x̄)) satisfies φ(g) = h_g g^{m(g)} h_g^{−1} with h_g ∈ π_1^et(X, x̄) and m(g) ∈ Ẑ^× for every g.
items.note: In each finite quotient via Čebotarev (Frobenius elements and decomposition groups), then a compactness argument.

items.name: Proposition 5.3: class preservation under (NR)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 5.1, φ is class-preserving: every element of π_1^et(X, x̄) is mapped to a conjugate.
items.locator: Proposition 5.3, p. 841; proof as corrected by E4
items.note: m(g) = 1 whenever the image of g under π_1^et(X) → G_k → Ẑ (a Ẑ-quotient of the cyclotomic character) generates an open subgroup; these elements are dense.

items.name: Lemma 5.4: ℓ-geometric covers of positive genus exhaust π₁ of a hyperbolic curve
items.statement: A connected pointed étale covering h: (X′, x̄′) → (X, x̄) is ℓ-geometric if π_1^et(X_k̄, x̄) acts on h^{−1}(x̄) through a finite ℓ-group. For ℓ ≠ char k and (C, c̄) a hyperbolic curve over k, π_1^et(C, c̄) is the union of the open subgroups H for which C_H → C is ℓ-geometric and C_H has smooth compactification of genus ≥ 1.
items.note: Checked the count: n_H ≤ (d/ℓ)(n − 1) + d with Riemann–Hurwitz gives 2g(C_H) − 2 ≥ (d/ℓ)((ℓ − 1)(n − 3) − 2) ≥ 1 once n ≥ 6.

items.name: Proposition 5.5: class preservation in general
items.statement: Let k be finitely generated over Q and X smooth geometrically connected, embeddable in a product of hyperbolic curves. For γ ∈ Aut_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et) with r(γ) = id_X, π_1(γ) ∈ OutAut_{G_k}(π_1(X)) is class-preserving.
items.note: Rational factors are replaced by ℓ-geometric covers of positive genus containing the image of a given σ (Lemma 5.4, with ℓ larger than the index of a normal subgroup in the image of π_1(X), so X′ stays geometrically connected). E6 is rejected as an alleged gap: the displayed embedding triangle gives r(γ′)=id by the construction/uniqueness defining r.

items.name: Lemma 5.6: class preservation by elements of the kernel
items.statement: Let 1 → Ḡ → G → Γ → 1 be an exact sequence of profinite groups and φ ∈ Aut_Γ(G). If for every open Γ′ ⊆ Γ the induced φ′ ∈ Aut_{Γ′}(p^{−1}(Γ′)) is class-preserving, then φ is class-preserving by elements of Ḡ.

items.name: Definition 6.1: strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods
items.statement: A strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhood over k is a smooth k-variety X with a tower X = X_n → ⋯ → X_1 → X_0 = Spec k in which each X_i → X_{i−1} is an elementary fibration into hyperbolic curves and each X_i embeds into a product of hyperbolic curves. Example: M_{0,n}, n ≥ 4 (forget points one at a time; forget all but four points in all ways). Over characteristic 0 they are of type K(π,1) by Proposition 2.8.

items.name: Theorem 6.2: the retraction is injective on strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods
items.statement: Let k be finitely generated over Q and X a strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhood over k. If γ ∈ Aut_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et) has r(γ) = id_X, then γ = id_{X_et}.
items.locator: Theorem 6.2, pp. 845–847; proof as corrected by E3
items.note: Induction along the tower: the induced δ on the base has r(δ) = id by Proposition 4.8; on the generic fibre Mochizuki's Theorem A gives g_η, which extends through the finite unramified Isom scheme.

items.name: Theorem 1.5: homotopy reconstruction of strongly hyperbolic Artin neighborhoods
items.statement: For k finitely generated over Q and strongly hyperbolic Artin neighborhoods X,Y over k, Isom_k(X,Y) → Isom_Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et(X_et,Y_et) is bijective.
items.note: Hoshi proves a similar statement in dimension ≤ 4 by other methods.

items.name: Lemma 6.3 and Corollary 1.7: anabelian Zariski neighbourhoods (Grothendieck's prediction)
items.statement: Every point of a smooth geometrically connected variety over an infinite perfect field has a fundamental system of Zariski-open strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods (Lemma 6.3). Hence every point of a smooth geometrically connected variety over k finitely generated over Q has a basis of Zariski neighbourhoods that are anabelian: k-isomorphisms between any two correspond bijectively to outer G_k-isomorphisms of their étale fundamental groups (Corollary 1.7).
items.note: Reject E7's claimed circular fibre definition: the published page distinguishes calligraphic universal 𝒮_𝒲 from S_W. The lemma has an infinite perfect base field; the anabelian consequence further requires k finitely generated over Q. A genuine later subscript slip is E14; it is distinct from the rejected alleged circular definition.

items.name: Constant-field rigidity for smooth varieties over finitely generated fields
items.statement: For a smooth geometrically connected variety X over a field k finitely generated over Q, the image of k in H⁰(X,O_X) is its unique maximal subfield. Consequently a scheme isomorphism between such X/k and Y/ℓ induces an isomorphism Spec k→Spec ℓ.
items.note: Restricted to the smooth finitely-generated characteristic-zero application of Theorem 7.1. The original unrestricted claim is false for nonreduced varieties (a derivation gives a second coefficient field in dual numbers). The multiplicative divisibility fact is separated below.

items.name: Theorem 1.8 and Theorem 7.1: the absolute version
items.statement: For k, ℓ finitely generated over Q and X/k, Y/ℓ smooth geometrically connected varieties embeddable in products of hyperbolic curves, Isom_Schemes(X, Y) → Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(X_et, Y_et) is a split injection with a functorial retraction, and a bijection if X and Y are strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods.
items.note: G_k is recovered as the quotient of π_1^et(X) by its maximal finitely generated closed normal subgroup; Pop's theorem identifies the base fields, and Theorems 1.2 and 1.5 apply over a fixed identification. The base-field isomorphism in the final base change points Spec(k)→Spec(ℓ), correcting E8.

items.name: Theorem 7.2: varieties that are not geometrically connected
items.statement: For k finitely generated over Q and smooth k-varieties X, Y each of whose connected components embeds in a product of hyperbolic curves over its field of constants, Isom_k(X, Y) → Isom_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) is a split injection with a functorial retraction, and a bijection if all components are strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods over their constant fields.
items.note: k-linearity of the constant-field isomorphism follows from Kummer theory: f_c^*(α) ≡ α mod (K^×)^n for all n.

items.name: Cofinite directed reindexing of pro-objects
items.statement: Every pro-object admits an isomorphic presentation indexed by the opposite of a cofinite directed set I; cofinite means {j | j<i} is finite. Transport morphisms by cofinal reindexing, with the Hom limit-colimit formula preserved.
items.note: Separated from /1; the appendix uses this for matching objects, G* and B*G.

items.name: Discrete classifying space is a K(G,1)
items.statement: For a discrete group G let BG be the nerve of its one-object groupoid. It is connected, π_1(BG)=G and π_n(BG)=0 for n≥2, naturally in G, using the simplicial/realization comparison.
items.note: H.1 states the realized K(G,1) theorem; Stage 8 supplies the comparison, rather than a second construction.

items.name: Discrete universal EG and the G-cover EG → BG
items.statement: For a discrete group G, EG is the nerve of the category with object set G and a unique arrow between any two objects. It is contractible; right multiplication acts freely, and EG → BG is a simplicial G-cover. Point EG at the identity.
items.note: Existing bar/group-homology objects are inputs, not a proved simplicial-cover identification.

items.name: Surjections of groups induce Kan fibrations of classifying spaces
items.statement: For a surjective homomorphism f:G′→G of discrete groups, Bf:BG′→BG is a Kan fibration; in particular BG is Kan, by taking G→1.
items.note: Do not confuse the definition of a Kan complex with this nerve lifting theorem.

items.name: Weak equivalences of connected pointed pro-spaces
items.statement: A map f:X→Y of connected pointed pro-spaces is an Isaksen weak equivalence iff π_n(f) is an isomorphism of pro-groups for every n≥1. The general disconnected statement requires homotopy pro-local systems, not merely a single base point.
items.locator: Corollary A.18 proof, p. 866; Isaksen 2001 Cor. 7.5
items.note: Separated the exact connected hypothesis from /4.

items.name: Cohomological detection of Isaksen weak equivalences
items.statement: A map f:X→Y of pro-spaces is a weak equivalence iff π_0(f) is an isomorphism of pro-sets, Π_1X→f*Π_1Y is an isomorphism of pro-local systems, and H^m(Y,L)→H^m(X,f*L) is an isomorphism for every m and every local system L on Y.
items.note: This is not detection by untwisted constant cohomology alone.

items.name: Properness, strong fibrations and strict homotopies into a fibrant target
items.statement: The Isaksen homotopy-pro-group model structure is proper; strong fibrations in its Definition 6.5 are fibrations. For a fibrant Y, maps X→Y modulo strict simplicial homotopy compute Hom_Ho(X,Y), since all X are cofibrant. The properness proof must use the correction in Isaksen 2004 Remark 4.14.
items.locator: Appendix pp. 853–854; Isaksen 2001 Props. 14.5, 17.1 and Hirschhorn 9.5.24
items.note: A provider bundle, not a checked proof of all cited source results; split and verify the corrected properness source before route 7 is accepted (G1/G3).

items.name: Proposition 2.4(b): geometric monodromy orbits
items.statement: Under the complete hypotheses of Proposition 2.4(a) (/12), the forgetful map factors through π_1^et(Y_k̄,ȳ)-orbits of pointed morphisms and the resulting map to unpointed morphisms over k_et is surjective.

items.name: Proposition 2.4(c): bijectivity under strong centre-freeness
items.statement: Under /12, if G_k is strongly centre-free, the surjection from geometric-monodromy orbits in Proposition 2.4(b) is bijective. The stabilizer of the structural map is trivial because its element centralizes an open image subgroup and thus the open subgroup it generates with that image.

items.name: Split closed points detect dominance of connected Galois covers
items.statement: For two connected finite étale Galois covers V_1,V_2 of the same regular connected arithmetic scheme 𝒳 as in /38, V_1 dominates V_2 iff every closed point splitting completely in V_1 splits completely in V_2. Equal splitting sets detect equality of their open normal subgroups, hence an isomorphism over 𝒳.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 5.1, p. 839, via Serre Thm. 7
items.note: Use Chebotarev in the common compositum. This is not a statement about arbitrary non-Galois covers.

items.name: Finite residue fields at closed points of arithmetic schemes
items.statement: Every closed point of a scheme of finite type over Z has finite residue field.
items.note: Separated from the Jacobson property; both are used to reduce factorization to finite-field points.

items.name: No infinitely divisible nonidentity units in finitely generated fields
items.statement: For a field K finitely generated over Q, ⋂_(n≥1) (K×)^n = {1}. Therefore if a,b∈K× have the same class modulo n-th powers for every n≥1, then a=b.
items.note: Use all positive n. This is not the assertion that K× has no torsion.

items.name: Theorem 1.1: Isom reconstruction for hyperbolic curves
items.statement: For a prime p, a sub-p-adic field k, and smooth hyperbolic k-curves X,Y, Isom_k(X,Y) → Isom_Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et(X_et,Y_et) is bijective.
items.note: Separated from the dominant Hom theorem.

items.name: Corollary 1.6: fundamental-group reconstruction of strongly hyperbolic Artin neighborhoods
items.statement: For k finitely generated over Q and strongly hyperbolic Artin neighborhoods X,Y over k, Isom_k(X,Y) → Isom_Gk^out(π_1^et(X),π_1^et(Y)) is bijective, where the outer quotient is by conjugation with geometric π_1(Y_k̄), not all arithmetic elements.
items.note: Separated from /70; uses K(π,1), the BG representation theorem and Proposition 2.4.

items.name: Bousfield–Kan homotopy-limit tower and convergence input
items.statement: For a pointed levelwise fibrant inverse diagram X, construct the cosimplicial replacement (Π*X)^n=∏_(i_n→⋯→i_0) X_(i_0), its genuine partial totalizations, and the homotopy-limit spectral sequence with E_2^(s,t)=lim^s π_t X in the allowed pointed-set/group ranges. Under π_0 X=* and profiniteness of π_t X for t≥1, verify the connectivity and complete-convergence hypotheses used to obtain π_t(holim X)≅lim π_t X; do not infer convergence merely from writing down an E_2-page.
items.locator: Theorem A.8 proof, pp. 857–858; BK XI §§5–7 and IX §§5.1,5.4; corrected E9
items.note: Added by independent review to expose an implicit dependency.

items.name: Relative simplicial cylinder for distinguished endpoints
items.statement: For a pro-simplicial set with two distinguished points, quotient X×Δ[1] by the two constant-point cylinders. The endpoint map X⊔_{ {0,1} }X→X∧I is a cofibration and projection X∧I→X is a weak equivalence. It computes endpoint-preserving homotopy classes into a fibrant target; the projection is not asserted to be a fibration.
items.note: Added by independent review to expose an implicit dependency.

items.name: Ordinary Kan–Quillen model structure required before the pro-model construction
items.statement: Equip simplicial sets with monomorphisms as cofibrations, Kan fibrations and weak homotopy equivalences, prove the closed simplicial model axioms and properness, and define the pointed variant. The abstract ModelCategory declaration and Kan predicate alone do not provide these theorems.
items.locator: Appendix p. 853 and the prerequisites of Isaksen's model construction
items.note: Added by independent review to expose an implicit dependency.

items.name: Étale cohomology continuity for affine inverse limits
items.statement: For the inverse system of finite field extensions k′ of k inside k̄ and a finite-type k-scheme X, étale cohomology of X_k̄ with an abelian local system descended to a finite stage is the filtered colimit of the cohomology over the later stages X_k′. Torsors and the finitely presented étale covering data descend to a finite stage. State the quasi-compact/quasi-separated and affine-transition hypotheses in any general extension.

routes.brief:
UNACCEPTED CANDIDATE — not a design instruction until G1–G8 are closed. Parent: Anabelian geometry and nonabelian Chabauty (AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty), importing NC.0 path torsors and NC.1 source-qualified curve reconstruction. The additional proposed foundation is Étale homotopy types and pro-spaces (EtaleHomotopyTypes), whose route is itself not accepted.

Endpoints, retaining the source hypotheses:
- For a sub-p-adic k and smooth hyperbolic k-curves X,Y, Theorem 1.1 identifies k-isomorphisms with isomorphisms of étale homotopy types over k_et. Theorem 3.2 separately identifies dominant morphisms from a smooth connected k-variety to a hyperbolic curve with π_1-open homotopy maps in its stated range.
- For k finitely generated over Q and X,Y smooth geometrically connected k-varieties each embeddable in a product of hyperbolic curves, Theorems 1.2/4.7 provide the unique functorial retraction on Isom, compatible with dominant maps to hyperbolic curves; a third variety Z in functoriality is also smooth.
- Under the same hypotheses on X, Theorem 1.9 says every kernel element induces a π_1-automorphism class-preserving by elements of the geometric fundamental group.
- For strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods X,Y over such k, Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 1.6 give bijectivity both for relative étale homotopy Isom and outer G_k-isomorphisms, quotienting by geometric conjugation.
- Lemma 6.3 provides a basis of strongly hyperbolic Artin open neighbourhoods over an infinite perfect field; the anabelian Corollary 1.7 further requires k finitely generated over Q.
- Theorem 7.1 gives the absolute Isom retraction for the same classes over finitely generated fields k,ℓ/Q, and bijectivity for strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods. Theorem 7.2 gives the relative k-version for smooth, not necessarily geometrically connected varieties whose individual components satisfy the product-embedding hypotheses over their constant fields.

Cover the hyperbolic-curve carrier, elementary/strongly hyperbolic Artin towers, §§4–7, the rational-point image separation and point-count factorization arguments, geometric class preservation, ℓ-covers with ℓ invertible and at least three punctures, finite-unramified relative Isom, constant fields and all-n Kummer injectivity. Keep the statements of the retraction clauses, corollaries and cited dependencies atomic. E6 is rejected: r(γ′)=id follows from the defining immersion argument, independently of uniqueness of γ′.

Import Scheme and stack foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/SF.2), Étale duality and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2:trace-purity and EDC.2:pairings), Inverse Galois and arithmetic fundamental groups (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1), relative Hom/Isom from Algebraic moduli for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2), and the existing Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves Layer 7 Hurwitz and ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9 Kummer plans. Unresolved imports must not be silently assigned to this Part II: Pop's birational field reconstruction; the full Hilbertian Galois-group consequence; arithmetic-scheme Chebotarev (not AN.4's number-field analytic interface); and smooth-variety compactification extending a map to a proper ambient variety (not R09.7d's quasi-projective resolution contract). Items /35 and /41 are quarantined in this rejected candidate solely to keep every missing item visible once, not to make this an owner for those general theories. R09.2 also needs a marked-boundary adapter from DM69's proper stable curves. Tests: punctured projective lines, products, M_0,5, finite-field point-count factors in unequal dimensions, geometric versus arithmetic Frobenius, and the direction Spec(k)→Spec(ℓ) in absolute reconstruction.
